200.title: Polish parliament approves ban on nighttime alcohol sales in shops
200.summary: Polish parliament approves ban on nighttime alcohol sales in shops Oct 9, 2026 | Business , Law , Politics , Society Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
200.body: Polish parliament approves ban on nighttime alcohol sales in shops Oct 9, 2026 | Business , Law , Politics , Society Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! An overwhelming majority of MPs in the Sejm, the lower house of Poland’s parliament, have voted in favour of a bill that would introduce tough new anti-alcohol measures, including a ban on all forms of advertising and on sales in shops during nighttime hours. Almost 200 Polish municipalities, including large cities such as Warsaw and Kraków , have already introduced their own local bans on nighttime alcohol sales. They also drank 82 litres of beer, down 18.7% since 2018 https://t.co/FxFMupWLRv — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 1, 2026 In June, an IBRiS poll for the Rzeczpospolita daily found that 55% of Poles support some form of ban on nighttime alcohol sales while 43% are opposed.

300.title: Allianz: Europe's Auto Industry Is Cutting in the Wrong Places
300.summary: The main cause of the decline is self-inflicted: Europe's auto industry has spent its money on the wrong things over the past two decades, according to the analysis.
300.body: The main cause of the decline is self-inflicted: Europe's auto industry has spent its money on the wrong things over the past two decades, according to the analysis. "When automakers finally shifted their capital to address future-oriented issues, it was spread too thinly across too many projects," said Guillaume Dejean, an auto industry expert at Allianz Trade. "The capital allocation decisions of the past two decades are a boomerang that is now coming back." Further market share losses threaten Allianz economists consider the situation facing Europe's auto industry highly concerning: Value added per vehicle sold in Europe has fallen by 30 to 45 percent since 2021/22, according to the analysis.
